study type: Experimental (in vivo and in vitro rat model)
outcome: Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers (TGF-b1, Smad2/Smad3, a-SMA, N-cadherin, Vimentin, E-cadherin, ZO-1, b-catenin, occludin)
cohort: The study involved male pups from time-mated Sprague-Dawley rats, whose penises were collected for in vivo analysis or cultured for in vitro treatment.
finding: Gestational DEHP exposure induced hypospadias in male rat pups by reducing urethral epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), which could be prevented by TGF-b1 through the activation of the TGF-b/Smad signal pathway.
